Source: TSE election results via Base dos Dados
(`br_tse_eleicoes.resultados_candidato_municipio_zona`), mayors, nine
Legal Amazon states, elections 2000-2024, queried on BigQuery 2026-10-09
(`_data/raw/tse/tse_mayoral_results_2000_2024.csv`; SQL in
`_scripts/sql/2026-10-09-tse-mayoral-results.sql`). The Dahis, de las Heras
and Saavedra (2026) replication file in `_data/raw/dahis-2026/` is an
external cross-check (identical votes on the Legal Amazon, ordinary
elections, 2000-2020, see `rebuild/05-reacquisition-controls.md` section 7)
and is not read here.
Pipeline script: `_scripts/03-controls-elections.R`.
Interim output: `_data/interim/tse_elections_2000_2024.rds` (2000-2020 until
phase 2, step 2.3).
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 03 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
tse_raw <- read_csv("_data/raw/tse/tse_mayoral_results_2000_2024.csv",
                    col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character())
tse <- read_rds("_data/interim/tse_elections_2000_2024.rds")
sample_geo <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds") %>%
  distinct(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation)
```

## Q1. What does the file contain?

What is checked: columns, elections and rounds, election types,
municipalities per election, empty codes, vote values.

```{r q1-shape}
names(tse_raw)
tse_raw %>% count(ano, turno) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = turno, values_from = n, names_prefix = "turno_")
tse_raw %>% mutate(ordinary = tipo_eleicao == "eleicao ordinaria") %>% count(ordinary)
tse_raw %>% filter(tipo_eleicao != "eleicao ordinaria") %>% count(ano, name = "supplementary_rows")
tse_raw %>% filter(tipo_eleicao == "eleicao ordinaria", turno == "1") %>%
  group_by(ano) %>% summarise(municipalities = n_distinct(id_municipio), rows = n(), .groups = "drop")
tse_raw %>% filter(!str_detect(id_municipio, "^[0-9]{7}$")) %>%
  select(ano, sigla_uf, id_municipio, id_municipio_tse, numero_candidato, votos)
tse_raw %>% summarise(votes_non_digit = sum(!str_detect(votos, "^[0-9]+$")),
                      numero_differs_from_party = sum(numero_candidato != numero_partido))
```

**Finding.** 17,374 rows, one per candidate x municipality x election x
round, summed over zones; all mayors; seven elections 2000-2024, second
rounds in a few large municipalities, 224 rows of supplementary elections
with free-text type labels. First-round ordinary elections cover 802-808
municipalities per year (the nine states, so the Legal Amazon extension of
task 1.1 is already in the file). The only empty municipality codes are
two 2024 rows of TSE code 73709 (MT), outside the window. Votes are
digits throughout; in 30 rows the ballot number differs from the party
number.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-d (first round, ordinary elections, 2000-2020
as constants).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-elections.R`, raw-state block (schema, office,
elections, rounds, states, digits, geocodes in the window).

## Q2. Which candidate key reproduces the inherited aggregation?

What is checked: the duplicate rows within municipality x election x
ballot number, and what summing over them does.

```{r q2-duplicates}
first_round <- tse_raw %>%
  filter(turno == "1", tipo_eleicao == "eleicao ordinaria", as.integer(ano) <= 2020)
dups <- first_round %>%
  group_by(ano, id_municipio, numero_candidato) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(ano, id_municipio, numero_candidato)
dups %>% count(ano, sigla_uf)
dups %>% select(ano, sigla_uf, id_municipio, sequencial_candidato, numero_candidato, sigla_partido,
                resultado, votos) %>% head(12)
dups %>% group_by(ano, id_municipio, numero_candidato) %>%
  summarise(same_votes = n_distinct(votos) == 1, same_party = n_distinct(sigla_partido) == 1,
            .groups = "drop") %>% count(same_votes, same_party)
```

**Finding.** Thirty-six municipality-elections of 2000 and 2004 carry two
rows for one ballot number, with two `sequencial_candidato` values and
identical votes and party: a Base dos Dados artefact. The lost script
grouped by `id_candidato_bd` and ballot number and summed, which doubled
these votes; summing by ballot number reproduces that count, and the
recovered panel's `elec_n_candidates` and `elec_enc` are reproduced on
every cell at the script 03 acceptance (commit message). The pipeline
keeps the sum and takes the smaller `sequencial_candidato` as the
winner's id.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-c (closed); the dedupe is a phase 2 entry.
**Assertion.** none (the duplicates are summed as inherited; KNOWN DEFECTS
block).

## Q3. Are uncontested elections coded as intended?

```{r q3-uncontested}
election_rows <- tse %>% filter(election_year == 1L, !is.na(elec_enc))
election_rows %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(municipalities = n(), uncontested = sum(elec_uncontested),
            mov_na = sum(is.na(elec_mov)), competitive_na = sum(is.na(elec_competitive)),
            .groups = "drop")
tse %>% filter(geocode == "1100031", year %in% 2008:2015) %>%
  select(year, election_year, elec_n_candidates, elec_enc, elec_mov, elec_competitive, elec_uncontested)
```

**Finding.** Uncontested races (7 to 29 per election) have ENC 1 and NA
margin and competitive flag in the election row, as intended. In phase 1
the stored panel carried them forward with `fill()`, which replaced the NA
margin and flag of an uncontested race with the previous election's
values (Cabixi, RO, 2012-2015): a code defect of the inherited storage,
reproduced on purpose then. Since phase 2, step 2.3 (2026-10-22) each year
is joined to its governing election and the NA persists over the four
governing years, as the Cabixi rows above now show (the 2012 race governs
2013-2016).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-d (definition); D-2026-10-22-d (storage).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-elections.R`, output block, on the election
rows (margin NA exactly when uncontested, ENC 1 when uncontested) and on
the stored rows (margin NA exactly when uncontested or no election).

## Q4. Is the election year mapped to the governing period correctly?

```{r q4-timing}
tse %>% filter(geocode == "1100015", year %in% 2003:2009) %>%
  select(year, election_year, elec_n_candidates, elec_enc, elec_winner_party)
```

**Finding.** In phase 1 the values changed in the election year itself
(the October 2004 result was stored from 2004), so a listing year such as
2008 carried the result of the election held that October, while the mayor
in office was elected in 2004: the off-by-one of task 1.5. Since phase 2,
step 2.3 (2026-10-22) the rows above show the governing rule: the 2004
result is stored from 2005 to 2008, the 2008 result from 2009, and
`election_year` still flags 2004 and 2008 themselves. Q7 holds the
evidence for the change.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-o (closed by D-2026-10-22-d).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-elections.R`, output block (every governing
year equals its election row; year minus governing election in 1-4; 2000
NA).

## Q5. How are the competitiveness measures distributed in the sample?

```{r q5-dist}
election_rows %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_candidates = mean(elec_n_candidates), mean_enc = mean(elec_enc),
            median_mov = median(elec_mov, na.rm = TRUE),
            share_competitive = mean(elec_competitive, na.rm = TRUE),
            share_uncontested = mean(elec_uncontested), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** Three candidates and 2.3 to 2.5 effective candidates on
average, a median margin of 10 to 12 points, and 43 to 49 percent of the
races below the ten-point threshold; the measures move little across
elections, with a rise in candidacies in 2020.
**Decision.** none required.

## Q6. Are there zero-vote candidates or first-place ties?

```{r q6-edge}
candidates <- first_round %>%
  group_by(geocode = id_municipio, year = as.integer(ano), numero_candidato, sigla_partido) %>%
  summarise(votes = sum(as.integer(votos)), .groups = "drop")
candidates %>% filter(votes == 0) %>% count(year)
candidates %>%
  group_by(geocode, year) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(votes), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(tie = votes[1] == votes[2], .groups = "drop") %>%
  count(tie)
```

**Finding.** Fifty-six candidates with zero votes, almost all in 2012
(candidacies refused after the ballot was printed); they enter the ENC and
the candidate count as inherited. No first-place tie, so the winner's
party and id are unambiguous.
**Decision.** none in phase 1; the zero-vote rows are for task 1.8.

## Q7. Does the governing-year storage reproduce the lagged block, and what do 2021-2024 hold? (phase 2, step 2.3, 2026-10-22)

What is checked: the governing election of each stored year; the stored
block against the phase 1 panel's one-year lag (`elec_*_gov`, built in
script 04 as a compensation for the election-year storage, D-2026-10-11-e)
on the biome sample; the municipality-years after 2000 without a governing
election; the 2021-2024 rows and the 2024 election.

```{r q7-map}
tse %>%
  distinct(year, elec_governing_year) %>%
  filter(!is.na(elec_governing_year)) %>%
  group_by(elec_governing_year) %>%
  summarise(governs = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q7-lag-equivalence}
# The comparison against the phase 1 lagged block was run at the step on
# the interim panel of 2026-10-22; once the _gov block is gone from the
# panel (D-2026-10-22-e) the chunk reports the recorded result instead.
phase1 <- read_rds("_data/interim/panel_amz_2000_2020.rds")
elec_vars <- c("elec_enc", "elec_mov", "elec_winner_share", "elec_n_candidates",
               "elec_winner_party", "elec_winner_id", "elec_competitive", "elec_uncontested")
if (!all(paste0(elec_vars, "_gov") %in% names(phase1))) {
  cat("Recorded at the step: zero differing cells in six of the eight columns;",
      "164 cells in elec_mov and in elec_competitive, all NA in the new storage",
      "where the lag carried a previous election's value onto an uncontested race.\n")
} else {
  cmp <- tse %>%
    select(geocode, year, all_of(elec_vars)) %>%
    inner_join(phase1 %>% select(geocode, year, all_of(paste0(elec_vars, "_gov"))),
               by = c("geocode", "year"))
  map_dfr(elec_vars, function(v) {
    a <- cmp[[v]]; b <- cmp[[paste0(v, "_gov")]]
    d <- xor(is.na(a), is.na(b)) | (!is.na(a) & !is.na(b) & a != b)
    tibble(variable = v, differing = sum(d), new_na_old_value = sum(d & is.na(a) & !is.na(b)))
  })
}
```

```{r q7-gaps}
sample_tse <- sample_geo %>%
  cross_join(tibble(year = 2000:2020)) %>%
  left_join(tse, by = c("geocode", "year"))
sample_tse %>%
  filter(year > 2000, is.na(elec_enc)) %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
tse_raw %>%
  filter(id_municipio %in% c("2100402", "2102150", "5104526", "5104542"), turno == "1") %>%
  distinct(id_municipio, ano) %>%
  group_by(id_municipio) %>%
  summarise(elections = paste(sort(ano), collapse = " "), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q7-extension}
tse %>%
  filter(year >= 2019) %>%
  group_by(year, election_year, elec_governing_year) %>%
  summarise(municipalities = n(), with_values = sum(!is.na(elec_enc)), .groups = "drop")
tse_raw %>%
  filter(ano == "2024", turno == "1", tipo_eleicao == "eleicao ordinaria") %>%
  summarise(municipalities = n_distinct(id_municipio), empty_code_rows = sum(id_municipio == ""))
```

**Finding.** Each stored year is joined to the election held in the last
October before it: the 2000 election governs 2001-2004, the 2020 election
2021-2024, and 2000 is NA because the 1996 election is outside the data.
On the biome sample the new storage equals the phase 1 lagged block cell
for cell in six of the eight columns; the margin and the competitive flag
differ on 164 cells, all of them uncontested races on which the lag had
carried the previous election's values (5 municipalities under the 2004
election, 7 under 2008, 20 under 2012, 4 under 2016, 12 under 2020, four
years each). After 2000, the only NA municipality-years are those without a
governing election in the file: Mojuí dos Campos 2001-2012 (installed
2013), and 2001-2004 for Ipiranga do Norte and Itanhangá (installed 2005)
and for Altamira do Maranhão and Brejo de Areia, which have no 2000
election in the extract; phase 1 stored them as NA too, because `fill()`
had nothing to carry. In 2021-2024, 807 of the 808 municipalities carry
the 2020 election; Macapá is NA because its 2020 election was postponed
to December after the Amapá blackout and the file types it
"eleicoes municipais 2020 - ap", which the ordinary-election filter of
D-2026-10-10-d excludes (within 2000-2020 the row is unaffected: Macapá's
2020 row holds the 2016 election under both storages). Whether that
postponed election counts as ordinary is a definition question left to
the author (flagged in D-2026-10-22-f). The 2024 election covers 805
municipalities with a code plus two rows with an empty code (the Boa
Esperança do Norte split) and governs 2025-2028, so it enters only
`election_year`.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-22-d (storage rule), D-2026-10-22-e (the `_gov`
block of script 04 retired), D-2026-10-22-f (series to 2024).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-elections.R`, output block (governing map and
equality with the election rows); `04-panel-assemble.R`, output block (28
NA municipality-years after 2000 on the 503-municipality panel).

## Q8. Who are the zero-vote candidates, and what does their exclusion move? (phase 2, step 2.7, 2026-10-28)

What is checked: the zero-vote candidates of Q6 by year and recorded
result, the sample's municipality-elections affected, and the pipeline
output after the exclusion (task 1.8; D-2026-10-28-e).

```{r q8-zero-vote}
zero <- first_round %>%
  group_by(geocode = id_municipio, year = as.integer(ano), numero_candidato, sigla_partido,
           numero_partido) %>%
  summarise(votes = sum(as.integer(votos)), resultado = paste(unique(resultado), collapse = "/"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(votes == 0)
zero %>% count(year, resultado)
zero_sample <- zero %>% filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode)
zero_sample %>% count(year)
affected <- zero_sample %>%
  distinct(geocode, year) %>%
  left_join(candidates %>% group_by(geocode, year) %>%
              summarise(n_all = n(), n_valid = sum(votes > 0), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("geocode", "year")) %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode")
affected %>% count(year, n_valid)
affected %>% filter(n_valid == 1) %>% select(municipality, state_abbreviation, year)
# Pipeline output after the fix (tse read at setup): the eight races are
# uncontested over their governing years.
tse %>%
  filter(geocode %in% affected$geocode[affected$n_valid == 1], year %in% 2013:2016) %>%
  summarise(cells = n(), uncontested = sum(elec_uncontested), mov_na = sum(is.na(elec_mov)),
            enc_one = sum(elec_enc == 1))
```

**Finding.** All 56 zero-vote candidates (54 in 2012, 2 in 2020) are
recorded as "não eleito", so the file carries no marker of the refused
candidacy beyond the zero. In the sample they sit in 37 elections of
2012 and in Magalhães Barata 2020; in eight 2012 races (Borba,
Tonantins, Uarini, Breves, Vigia, Aragominas, Itaúba, Matupá) the
zero-vote candidate was the only opponent. Excluding them leaves the ENC
and the winner's share unchanged (a zero share adds nothing), lowers
`elec_n_candidates` in 148 cells of the final panel (37 municipalities,
2013-2016) and makes the eight races uncontested, so their margin and
competitive flag are NA and `elec_uncontested` is 1 over 2013-2016
(`compare_outputs`, commit message of step 2.7).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-28-e.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-elections.R`, output block (56 zero-vote
candidates dropped, every remaining candidate has votes, no election
lost).
